title: Ruby Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Print a message
entries.summary: puts prints a value and moves to a new line. Quoted letters make a string.

entries.name: Keep a named number
entries.summary: Ruby variables give names to values. The plus sign adds numbers.
notes: Do not put number values in quotes when you want maths.

entries.name: Put a value in text
entries.summary: Inside double quotes, #{name} places a value into text.

entries.name: Make a choice
entries.summary: if runs a block when its rule is true. Ruby closes this block with end.

example.code:
score = 8
if score >= 5
  puts "Pass"
else
  puts "Try again"
end

notes: Remember the final end for the if block.

entries.name: Read a list item
entries.summary: An array keeps values in order. The first index is zero.
notes: An index past the list gives nil, not a new item.

entries.name: Repeat with a block
entries.summary: each visits each item. The name between vertical bars is the current item.
notes: Use the current item n inside the block.

entries.name: Write a method
entries.summary: A method is a named set of steps. Ruby returns the last expression by default.

example.code:
def twice(n)
  n * 2
end
puts twice(4)

notes: Keep the calculation as the last expression if it is the answer.

entries.name: Find a value by label
entries.summary: A hash pairs keys with values. :title is a symbol used as a key.

example.code:
book = { title: "Moon Trip", pages: 24 }
puts book[:title]

notes: The symbol :title and the string "title" are different keys.

entries.name: Change every item
entries.summary: map makes a new array from the result of a block for each item.
notes: map returns a new array; it does not replace the old one.

entries.name: Handle no value
entries.summary: nil means no value. The || operator chooses the right side when the left side is nil or false.
notes: Zero and empty strings count as true in Ruby.

entries.name: Make a small object
entries.summary: A class groups data and methods. initialize runs when a new object is made.
notes: @colour belongs to the object; colour is only a local input.

entries.name: Handle an expected error
entries.summary: rescue handles an error of a named kind. Integer tries to read a whole number from text.

example.code:
begin
  puts Integer("cat")
rescue ArgumentError
  puts "Use a whole number"
end

notes: Handle the error you expect instead of hiding every error.
